question: India follows an opt-out (presumed consent) system for deceased organ donation under THOTA, meaning all citizens are presumed to have consented to organ donation unless they have formally registered an objection.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. India has an opt-in system under THOTA — consent must be actively given. Presumed consent (opt-out) is used in countries like Spain and Wales. In India, family consent is typically required even when a donor card exists, which further reduces effective donation rates.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. India operates an opt-in system under THOTA, meaning consent must be affirmatively given — either by the donor before death (donor card, registry) or by the next of kin after death. There is no presumed consent. India's opt-in system is one of the reasons for its relatively low deceased donation rates compared to countries like Spain and Wales which have opt-out systems.
